title: Room for a Rest
stylePrompt: Original vocal cool-jazz hotel-lounge song, about 2:30, 82 BPM relaxed brushed 4/4 swing, Dry warm tenor sax, upright bass, sparse piano and soft brushes; intimate wooden-room sound and warm tape, Clean low-to-mid male baritone, young-adult timbre, cool straight tone, deadpan, crisp English consonants and a tiny private smile, Aloof and self-possessed, never an elderly crooner: no smoky rasp, gravel, growl, heavy vibrato or belting, Restrained verses and an elegant memorable hook; let the hotel-etiquette jokes land without mugging, One concise two-bar double-time tenor display, one bar of nimble light scat, then one full-band silent bar; immediately regain composure, Sparse vocal phrasing, deliberate gaps and a complete quiet ending, Aim for the 52-bar arrangement in the lyrics, No choir, EDM, borrowed standard melody or named-performer imitation
lyrics:
[Intro - 4 bars, tenor, brushed drums and upright bass; no vocal]

[Verse 1 - 8 bars, restrained]
I don't talk. The tenor signs my name.
The desk asks, "Floor?" I give it half a beat.
I tip the bell for keeping to itself.
It rings once. Some people can't be discreet.

[Chorus - 8 bars]
Room for a rest. Leave a little space.
Hang a "Do Not Hurry" on the bass.
If silence needs a reason to stay,
Put it on my bill. I'll look away.

[Verse 2 - 8 bars]
The grand piano asks me for a key.
I leave a B-flat underneath the mat.
The carpet bows. I bow a little lower.
We both agree to leave it there at that.

[Chorus - 8 bars]
Room for a rest. Leave a little space.
Hang a "Do Not Hurry" on the bass.
If silence needs a reason to stay,
Put it on my bill. I'll look away.

[Break - 4 bars: two-bar double-time tenor burst, one-bar light scat, one full-band silent bar]
Doo-bid-a, ba-dip, da-bop.
[One full bar of silence]

[Bridge - 4 bars, back to an unhurried deadpan]
Pardon the flourish.
A note fell out.
I put it back.
No need to shout.

[Final Chorus - 6 bars]
Room for a rest. Leave a little space.
Hang a "Do Not Hurry" on the bass.
Put it on my bill. I'll look away.

[Outro - 2 bars, dry stop and a soft tenor tag]
The bell can show you out.
I'll stay in.

title: Crooked Little Line
stylePrompt: 1950s hotel jump-jazz meets rockabilly, warm vintage small-band recording with dry room ambience; expressive, confident female lead with playful crisp English diction, wide range climbing into the top notes, stacked harmonies widening each repeated hook chorus, layered upper voices swelling over group 'hey' responses, then a lone lead before the final harmony stack; upbeat 144 BPM swinging 4/4, spirited and mischievous; slapping upright bass drives the hook, brisk drums and dry handclaps, clean twangy electric guitar, short punchy horn replies; two compact verses, 16-bar slap-bass break, short bridge, clean stop-time ending; target 2:25–2:45
lyrics:
[Intro - 4 bars, slap bass and handclaps]

[Verse 1]
The carpet whispers, "Walk politely."
The elevator keeps the beat.
I brought a bass that's taller than me
And put the lobby on its feet.

[Chorus]
Crooked little line, go left, go right,
Put a little dent in a perfect night.
Click goes the heel, slap goes the string,
Even the arrows wanna swing.
Hey! If the sign says "stand in line,"
I'll stand beside it, looking fine.

[Verse 2]
The concierge mislaid his pencil,
The clock fell half a beat behind.
I signed the bill "a little sideways" —
They charged me for a crooked line.

[Chorus]
Crooked little line, go left, go right,
Put a little dent in a perfect night.
Click goes the heel, slap goes the string,
Even the arrows wanna swing.
Hey! If the sign says "stand in line,"
I'll stand beside it, looking fine.

[Instrumental Break - 16 bars, slap bass and horn replies]

[Bridge]
Let straight wait till the morning,
Let quiet take a chair.
I tied a bow around the rulebook;
Now it's dancing in the air.

[Final Chorus]
Crooked little line, go left, go right,
Put a little dent in a perfect night.
Click goes the heel, slap goes the string,
Even the arrows wanna swing.
Hey! If the sign says "stand in line,"
I'll stand beside it, looking fine.

[Outro - stop time]
One more little crooked line.
Room service? We're doing fine.

title: Velvet Has Teeth
stylePrompt: Swing song, young girl-child female lead in clear high treble and light pure head voice, with clipped rhythmic staccato phrasing, smiling, crisp English diction and minimal vibrato; poised, playful delivery in a 108 BPM swung 4/4 minor-key groove with sly chromatic turns; muted electric swing guitar leads with short tremolo chords and a brief interlude, sparse pizzicato upright bass, soft brushed snare, low clarinet, tiny music-box tones and a signature bell before the vocal; roomy, unprocessed vocals in a sweet-but-dangerous theatrical late-night 1960s hotel cabaret mix; two short verses, hook chorus, thin music-box bridge, final chorus, single-bell ending, 2:35–2:50
lyrics:
[Intro - a single bell, then muted guitar]

[Verse 1]
I wear a ribbon round the thunder,
A little bell beside the storm.
The room is full of velvet whispers;
I keep the sharp ones soft and warm.

[Chorus]
Velvet has teeth and sugar has a switch,
Tiny little bell, pretty little glitch.
No bark, all bite — click, goodnight.
I borrow the dark and I pocket the light.
Sweet little shoes, wicked little art:
There's a rabbit with a riot in its heart.

[Verse 2]
The moon slips coins into my pocket,
The lobby clock forgets to chime.
I leave a heart upon the room key
And charge the dark for overtime.

[Chorus]
Velvet has teeth and sugar has a switch,
Tiny little bell, pretty little glitch.
No bark, all bite — click, goodnight.
I borrow the dark and I pocket the light.
Sweet little shoes, wicked little art:
There's a rabbit with a riot in its heart.

[Instrumental Interlude - 8 bars, electric swing guitar]

[Bridge - music box, almost whispered]
Smile like a secret,
Step like a hush.
If you ask who runs this ballroom —
Hear the bell. Don't rush.

[Final Chorus]
Velvet has teeth and sugar has a switch,
Tiny little bell, pretty little glitch.
No bark, all bite — click, goodnight.
I borrow the dark and I pocket the light.
Sweet little shoes, wicked little art:
There's a rabbit with a riot in its heart.

[Outro - one bell]
No bark, all bite.
A velvet little goodnight.
